newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace is to sue over EU imports of gene maize.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace is to sue over EU imports of gene maize.

text.p: Environmentalist group Greenpeace was planning to sue importers, shipowners and authorities which allowed U.S. gene-modified maize into the European Union in breach of current rules, campaigner Benny Haerlin said.
"We've been told about these arrivals by the U.S. authorities and we've asked our lawyers to take action," he told a press conference.
Apart from a 34,000 tonne cargo of maize possibly containing the new variety and believed to have reached Germany, Greenpeace also had information such maize had arrived in Italy and the Netherlands.
News emerged last week U.S. gene-modified maize may have arrived in Spain and Portugal.
Greenpeace says too little is known about possible environmental effects of the new strain and a "marker gene" used in the new maize could lower antibiotic resistance in humans and animals.
The EU Commission is due to decide on December 18 whether to allow imports of such modified maize, made by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG.
Until then, it is illegal to market it in the EU.
U.S. exporters do not separate this maize, altered to resist the corn borer pest and certain weedkillers and estimated to amount to 0.6 percent of the U.S. crop, from the ordinary variety.

"I want the EU to deny clearance, if they can't resist what is admittedly strong U.S. pressure, they might as well hand over all responsibility to the U.S. authorities in the first place," Haerlin said.
